correctness.rationale: Finite Boolean powerset endomorphisms are exactly inverse image maps f^{-1} for unique f:X→X. Modal Diamond preservation is equivalent to f[R(x)]=R(f(x)), and for finite S5 equivalence clusters each source cluster must surject onto one entire target cluster. The surjection count q_ij=a_j!S(a_i,a_j) yields unrestricted image polynomial E_X by inclusion-exclusion over occupied target clusters, and idempotent polynomial I_X by fixing selected image clusters pointwise. An omitted smallest source cluster cannot map onto larger targets, so idempotent retraction support is realizable iff it contains at least one globally smallest cluster. Thus support count 2^m−2^(m−r), rank support equality, image isomorphism-type count c_a·prod_{b>a}(c_b+1). Independent enumeration of all selfmaps in profiles (1,1),(1,2),(1,2,3),(2,2) verified full algebra-image ranks, idempotent counts and supports, including (1,2,3) polynomials E=z²+20z⁸+6z¹⁶+12z⁶⁴ and I=z²+7z⁸+z¹⁶+z⁶⁴. Symbolic proof covers every finite nonempty equivalence frame.

Monteiro et al. 2006 counts all subalgebras, not individual idempotents or dual supports; full text also unavailable. value.rationale: The complete rank polynomials for arbitrary unequal S5 cluster sizes, their equality-of-attainable-ranks despite unequal multiplicities, and the minimum-cluster anchor criterion classify a natural finite modal-algebra endomorphism/retraction invariant. This distinguishes dual map supports from embedded algebra images and gives explicit computations for finite monadic Boolean algebras rather than an arbitrary tiny example.
